source_text: Anopheles arabiensis were tested as 1st generation offspring (F1) of wild collected adult mosquitoes from cattle sheds in Lower Moshi. Resistance testing using WHO cylinders in November 2011 shortly prior to the experimental hut trial showed resistance to pyrethoids but full susceptibility to dichlorodiphenyl-trichloroethane (DDT) and fenitrothion (Table 4).

coord_source_text: An experimental hut trial was conducted at KCMUCo Field Station in Lower Moshi Rice Irrigation Zone (3°22'S, 37°19'E) where An. arabiensis was the major malaria vector [24].
source_text: After the experimental hut trial a sub-sample of 80 An. arabiensis, that were collected alive from the hut with alpha ITN, were tested for the presence of L1014F and L10145S kdr variants. No kdr mutations were detected, confirming earlier reports of metabolic resistance mechanisms [26].
